result.comment: Two stories keep this bounded: share workflow mechanics and convert Research, then extract its brief activity and prove reuse. No open owner questions. Plan workflows, backward compatibility and production activation remain out of scope. Recommend /implement follow the two-story plan. Publication and readiness remain pending factory terminal processing.

plan.summary: Refactor existing workflow mechanics into lf_agent, lf_if, lf_loop, lf_comment and lf_ask with a small explicit mode policy; fully convert Research and extract lf_research_brief for its two documents. Prove reuse through a second-mode test package. Keep existing durable records, permission and owner-approval boundaries; no compatibility, Plan implementation or new framework.

stories.title: Share workflow mechanics and convert Research to generic actions

user_story.want: reuse the same execution, branching, reporting and owner-question mechanisms across modes
user_story.benefit: new workflows need role files and a graph rather than copied runtime code
notes: This is a bounded extraction of existing behavior. Research keeps its vocabulary and presentation; another mode is exercised only by tests.

Evidence inventory: AC-001 and AC-003 use offline registry, capture, source-control and graph-policy tests; AC-006 uses runner fakes and durable local-store recovery tests; AC-008 uses old-capture/non-graph regression tests and repository checks. Existing co-located tests are available. Evidence is bound to the implementation snapshot; checks remain to be executed. No authentic provider observation is claimed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Register lf_agent, lf_if, lf_loop, lf_comment and lf_ask through one shared implementation per mechanism and a small explicit mode policy. Admission retains mode authorization and rejects unknown actions, old Research mechanism names and scoped actions not registered for the admitted mode; generic spelling alone grants no authority.

Shared controls retain true/false outcomes, current identity-checked source decoding, initial defaults only before any source attempt, durable limits and owner-wait path rules. Invalid sources, malformed output, exhausted bounds and paths bypassing required waits reject or fail with their actual diagnostic; they cannot silently advance.

Extract common package capture, role delivery, admission, agent invocation, result retention, reporting, owner waits and continuation/recovery behind explicit mode policy. Tests preserve admitted permissions, attempt/run and metering identities, refused-resume cold fallback, candidate/delivery identities and actual failures. Only lf_ask opens a durable owner wait; acknowledgment-loss/restart tests reconcile retained delivery without repeating an acknowledged effect.

Convert shipped Research mechanism registrations, DOT and relevant captured role instructions to generic actions with no old-name aliases, compatibility decoders, migration or automatic deletion. Unsupported pre-cutover captures fail clearly before dispatch/effects. Non-graph Research and activation defaults remain unchanged. Run make check successfully and confirm gofmt -l . is empty.

tasks.description: Extract the small static mode policy, shared registry/source controls and package capture; keep explicit ActionSpec mode checks and Research result/presentation adapters.
Share activities and lifecycle through request, provider, store and daemon seams; convert Research generic actions/assets together, reject old captures and preserve non-graph/default behavior.
Add focused registry, source/default, graph-policy, package and injected-runner regression tests with external dependencies faked.
Extend normal untagged temporary-store recovery tests for wait/delivery identity, acknowledgment loss and continuation; verify old-capture and non-graph/default regressions.
Resolve failures, run make check and confirm empty gofmt -l . output; retain actual execution evidence.

architecture.summary: Extract within current package owners using per-admitted-mode registries and function-valued policy seams. Keep the existing engine, records and scoped Research contract.

components.name: internal/graphexec and internal/teamsource
components.responsibility: Pure action/path validation and bounded owned-package capture with explicit mode and role/resource closure.

components.name: internal/turn, internal/agent and provider adapters
components.responsibility: Shared invocation, source controls, result retention and report/ask lifecycle; Research supplies decoding, vocabulary and presentation.

components.name: internal/store and internal/daemon
components.responsibility: Existing durable admission, delivery, authenticated reply and continuation mechanics parameterized by admitted mode.

interfaces.name: Per-mode registry and policy
interfaces.input: Admitted mode, registered actions, response decoder/validator, presentation and owner-gate policy
interfaces.output: Authorized generic graph and shared activity implementations

interfaces.name: Shared delivery
interfaces.input: Retained source/candidate and report or question/review kind
interfaces.output: Existing published outcome and retained effect identity; durable wait only for ask

constraints: Preserve physical tables and single-connection SQLite ownership; no new package, framework or database redesign.
Keep bounded package reads, permission intersection, context/cancellation and existing failure policy.
Preserve one agent stage per run and durable next-stage dispatch; production registration remains Research-only.
No protected .claude or .codex instruction-tree edits are identified; update captured Research assets and applicable shared documentation.

decisions.decision: Keep one registry per admitted mode and preserve ActionSpec.Mode checks.
decisions.reason: Generic names remove the naming fence but need no multi-mode plugin registry.

decisions.decision: Allow existing Research document generation through its policy as an intermediate step until US-002 extracts it.
decisions.reason: US-001 remains runnable; final feature completion requires the explicit brief activity in US-002.

stories.title: Make Research brief generation explicit and prove workflow reuse

user_story.want: both Research documents generated from the same candidate before it is reported or handed onward
user_story.benefit: documents stay coherent while reusable workflow mechanics remain independent of Research
notes: Investigation and shaping remain Markdown roles. One scoped activity owns both documents; no general document framework or additional Plan workflow is introduced.

Evidence inventory: AC-004 uses pure policy/rendering tests plus actual temporary-file unsafe-path, replay and partial-write tests; AC-005 uses assembled Research with a real temporary SQLite store and injected runner/transport; AC-002 and AC-007 use captured second-mode/file-only-role fixtures and repository checks. Existing writer, capture, turn, daemon and store test patterns are available. All evidence is implementation-snapshot-bound and awaits execution; synthetic fixtures do not certify live Claude/Codex operation.

acceptance_criteria.text: Register Research-only lf_research_brief and remove document generation from lf_agent. It resolves a named retained candidate, validates safe destinations before writes, generates RESEARCH_BRIEF.md and RESEARCH_TECHNICAL.md only inside the admitted session, then validates references/artifacts and retains source-bound success or an actionable failure. Payload declarations and pre-existing artifacts are checked before result retention; only these two generated documents defer existence checks. Replaying the same candidate reproduces content. Partial writes, unsafe paths, artifact failures or a mismatched candidate cannot release success. Graph admission and consumption require matching successful generation before every successful Research report, ask/review or stage handoff; failure diagnostics may bypass it.

The assembled converted Research graph preserves investigation, shaping, questions, reviews, final reporting and authenticated candidate/stage-bound owner approval. Each successful question/review/report or handoff uses current generated documents. Worker done/approved output, stale replies and duplicate replies cannot create approval or duplicate continuation; old files or another candidate's brief success cannot satisfy the document gate.

A small test-only second-mode package uses the same capture, role delivery, agent/control/comment/ask and continuation/recovery implementations as Research, with its own existing-shaped result policy and vocabulary. It requires no copied handlers or role-specific runtime branch, exercises durable owner waits and restart handling, and generates no Research documents. It adds no production Plan registration or workflow.

A fixture adds a Markdown role and DOT node using an existing contract and permissions without a new handler or role-specific runtime branch. Shipped Research DOT and captured role instructions reflect the explicit brief boundary and generic mechanisms. Execute the assembled regression tests, make check successfully and confirm gofmt -l . is empty; retain results as offline behavior evidence only.

tasks.description: Extract the scoped brief activity, split declaration/pre-existing-artifact checks from generated-document checks, enforce safe writes and source-bound success, and update both Research stages and report/handoff validation.
Add pure document-rendering, source-binding and graph-policy tests for generated-file exemptions, deterministic content and bypass rejection.

Extend normal untagged assembled tests using temporary files and real migrated SQLite with injected runners/transport: unsafe and partial writes, Research owner gates, second-mode wait/restart reuse and file-only role addition.
Fix regressions, complete captured Research documentation and run make check plus gofmt -l .; retain actual aggregate check evidence.

architecture.summary: A concrete Research effect reuses existing renderers and artifact validation. Successful generation is a retained candidate-bound prerequisite, not merely the presence of files.

components.name: internal/turn/research_briefs.go and research_artifacts.go
components.responsibility: Generate and validate the two documents with safe destinations and candidate-bound outcome.

components.name: Research policy in internal/graphexec and internal/turn
components.responsibility: Enforce generation on successful report/ask/handoff paths while permitting failed-agent diagnostics.

components.name: internal/teamsource/research and co-located tests
components.responsibility: Wire both Research stages and demonstrate the shared runtime with a test-only second package.

interfaces.name: lf_research_brief
interfaces.input: Named retained Research source, current candidate/attempt identity and admitted session
interfaces.output: success with both source-bound artifact references or failed with actionable diagnostic

interfaces.name: Research successful-consumer prerequisite
interfaces.input: Consumer source identity and retained brief output
interfaces.output: Matching generation permission or explicit rejection

constraints: Controls continue to read the agent result, not the brief output.
Validate destination safety before writing; partial files may remain but never count as completed generation.
Use existing normal test conventions: no integration build tag or _Integration test name, no paid provider execution.
No remote publication, owner approval or mode-transition authority is granted by document generation.

decisions.decision: One activity produces both Research documents.
decisions.reason: They describe one candidate and reuse the current renderers without a generic document system.

decisions.decision: Deterministic writes plus retained source-bound success are sufficient.
decisions.reason: Recovery must block downstream success after partial failure, but needs no cross-file transaction framework.
